title: PickMe card catalogue
description: Documents the shape of card-catalogue.json exactly as decoded by Engine/Sources/CardCopilotEngine/Models/CatalogueModels.swift — it does not redesign the shape (spec §4). Two distinct 'unused' markers appear below: "x-status": "declared-not-computed" means the field IS a Swift struct property but no scoring/matching logic (RuleMatcher, Scorer, CapMath, PortfolioAnalyzer) ever reads it; "x-status": "documentation-only" means the field has NO corresponding Swift property at all, so JSONDecoder silently drops it on load — it is pure human-facing metadata. Two behaviors are engine-defined rather than data-defined: ownerConditions ids and the pseudo-categories/categoryParents RuleMatcher special-cases. This schema enumerates their current legal values; adding a new one is an engine code change, not a catalogue edit. program.programId used to be a third — the Scorer switched its valuation dispatch on that string — but since 2026-08-20 valuations are keyed data (programs.json, overridable per programId by owner state) and the Scorer dispatches on the valuation's model instead.

catalogueVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. Load-bearing: SeedLoader.validate(catalogueVersion:) parses MAJOR and throws SeedLoaderError.unsupportedCatalogueVersion if it isn't a MAJOR this build recognizes (currently only 1). Bump MAJOR on any breaking shape change, MINOR on additive/compatible ones; every edit gets a CHANGELOG.md entry (spec §3).

currency.description: Catalogue-wide reporting currency. Not per-card; individual purchases can still be USD (see PurchaseContext.currency in engine-fixtures.schema.json).

_provenance.description: Free-text sourcing note. No Catalogue.provenance property exists in Swift.

programId.description: The key a card's rewards currency is valued under. Hoisted into $defs on 2026-08-20 so programs.schema.json can reference the one list instead of keeping a second copy in step. Since that date this is a DATA key, not an engine dispatch key: Scorer.valueCad switches on the valuation's model, so a new programId needs an entry in programs.json (or an owner-state override) and no engine code change. A programId with neither has no valuation. NOTE: as of this bump Scorer.valueCad still returns 0.0 for it rather than excluding the card — the current gap is pinned in CatalogueIntegrityTests.knownUnvaluedPrograms and closing it is separate work.

cardProduct.description: Mirrors CardProduct — every listed property below is non-optional in Swift and therefore required here.

^_.description: Free-text annotation (e.g. _note). Not decoded by the engine.

network.description: Network enum. A purchase's acceptedNetworks must contain this or Scorer excludes the card outright (Warning.networkNotAccepted).

fxRules.description: RuleMatcher.activeFxRule picks the first entry whose effectiveFrom/effectiveTo window covers asOf; later entries let an announced future rate coexist with the current one.

perTransactionRewardVisibility.description: Free String in Swift, not an enum — these three are the catalogue's current convention, not a type-level constraint.

sources.description: Issuer source URLs. CardProduct has no `sources` property.

stacking.description: Free-text stacking note (e.g. MBNA's five independent $50k caps). Not decoded.

categoryMccReference.description: Human MCC-to-category lookup table (Tangerine). Not decoded; RuleMatcher never reads it.

redemptionFactors.description: Documented redemption boost factors (e.g. Rogers' 1.5x service redemption). Not decoded and not scored in v1 — see the factor's own _note.

credits.description: Optional. Absent for most cards; absence means no credits, never unknown.

fee.description: Every field optional in Swift's Fee struct.

status.description: Decoded onto FxRule.status but RuleMatcher.activeFxRule selects purely by effectiveFrom/effectiveTo window, never by this field.

announcedAt.description: FxRule has no `announcedAt` property — dropped silently on decode.

freeAllowanceCadPerCalendarMonth.description: When present, Scorer only appends Warning.fxAllowanceAssumed — it does not net the allowance out of fxCost.

postAllowanceRate.description: Decoded onto FxRule.postAllowanceRate but Scorer never applies it; fxCost is either 0 (allowance present) or amountCad * rate (no allowance), regardless of this value.

sourceType.description: Unlike EarnRule.sourceType, FxRule has NO sourceType property in Swift at all — this key is present in every JSON record but silently dropped on decode.

lastVerifiedAt.description: FxRule has no `lastVerifiedAt` property — dropped silently on decode (contrast CardProduct.lastVerifiedAt and EarnRule.lastVerifiedAt, which are both real).

status.description: Decoded onto EarnRule.status but RuleMatcher.isLive only checks effectiveFrom/effectiveTo/scoredInV1 — this field never gates anything.

ownerConditions.description: OPEN vocabulary, same rules as benefits-catalogue.schema.json's family/kind — deliberately NOT a closed enum. RuleMatcher.conditionsResolveTrue switches on the known strings above and treats any unknown id as unresolved (fails closed), so unrecognised ids decode fine and simply never match rather than rejecting the whole catalogue load. A closed enum here is exactly what let amazonEligiblePrimeLinked ship with no RuleMatcher case and no schema complaint; opening it doesn't add a handler, but it stops the schema from claiming one exists. A new id still requires an engine code change to actually gate on.

scoredInV1.description: false excludes the rule from RuleMatcher.isLive regardless of dates. Absent means true. Deprecated: a hand-set boolean carries no machine-readable reason and can't turn itself on when its blocker is fixed. New disabled rules should use requires or outOfScope instead; scoredInV1: false without either is only valid for a rule whose blocker is still unconfirmed (see the rule's _note).

requires.description: Engine capabilities this rule needs, matching EngineCapability's raw values (Engine/Sources/CardCopilotEngine/Models/EngineCapability.swift). RuleMatcher.isLive treats the rule as live only if every named capability is in EngineCapability.supported; an unrecognised or unsupported string skips the rule, same as scoredInV1: false did. Absent means no capability is needed. Turns the rule on automatically the day the named capability ships — no catalogue edit required. Mutually exclusive with outOfScope.

reason.description: Why this rule will never be scored by this engine, e.g. an online booking channel PickMe (an at-the-register copilot) does not cover. Human-facing; RuleMatcher.isLive only checks presence, not content.

outOfScope.description: Set when the rule is permanently out of scope — never to be built, as distinct from requires' "not yet". RuleMatcher.isLive always returns false when this is present, regardless of requires or scoredInV1. Mutually exclusive with requires: a rule ruled out permanently must not also declare a capability it is waiting on.

sourceType.description: Decoded onto EarnRule.sourceType (a real Swift property, unlike FxRule's copy of this same key) but never read by any matching or scoring logic.

earn.description: Union on `type`, matching the Earn enum's custom Codable implementation.

premiumCentsPerLitre.description: Earn.centsPerLitre carries no associated value in Swift; the custom decoder reads only `type` for this case and ignores every other key.

oneOf.description: Informational only — Scorer.rawEarn maps this case to -1, and any rule using it (see triangle-fuel-cpl) also sets scoredInV1: false. Needs litres to value, which the catalogue doesn't carry.

predicate.description: Every field optional in Swift's Predicate struct. An empty object {} matches any purchase (base rule).

categories.description: Purchase-category strings, PLUS two engine-defined pseudo-categories RuleMatcher.matches special-cases: "recurring" (checks PurchaseContext.recurringIndicator, ignoring the purchase's actual category) and "ownerSelectedTangerineCategory" (checks CardState.selectedCategories). Also subject to RuleMatcher.categoryParents expansion — currently only "marriottDirect" implies ["lodging", "travel"], so a predicate listing the parent still matches the more specific purchase category.

mccInclude.description: When present alongside `categories` and the purchase has a known MCC, the MCC must also be in this list. A nil/unknown purchase MCC falls back to matching on category alone (the permissive-fallback path).

merchantExclude.description: Checked before mccInclude/categories — a brand exclusion wins even if the MCC would otherwise qualify (see Costco vs Triangle grocery).

recurringViaNetworkIndicator.description: Decoded onto Predicate.recurringViaNetworkIndicator but RuleMatcher.matches never reads it — the actual recurring gate is the "recurring" pseudo-category checking PurchaseContext.recurringIndicator directly.

period.description: Read by PortfolioAnalyzer for monthly-cap reporting and by Swift cap-window projections. MoneyTalks additionally resolves the current server ledger window from this field.

anchor.description: Decoded onto Cap.anchor (a self-documenting pointer string like "ownerState.scotiaAccountYearAnchorMonth"). MoneyTalks resolves the declared owner-state anchor for account-year ledger windows; Swift cap-window projections resolve the same supported paths.

resetTimeZone.description: Decoded onto Cap.resetTimeZone but the engine never computes a period rollover, so this is never read.

proration.description: Decoded onto Cap.proration but CapMath.split always splits a straddling purchase proportionally, unconditionally — this flag is never branched on.

cardCredit.description: A recurring statement credit granted for holding the card. NOT an earn rule: a credit does not depend on what the purchase was, so it never enters the checkout pick — it is keep/cancel and net-value input only. valueCad is the issuer's stated maximum, not a forecast of use; whether it was redeemed is owner activity and lives with the consumer.

period.description: Same vocabulary as cap.period; decoded into Swift's CapPeriod.

sources.description: Issuer pages the amount and period were read from. Required when sourceType is issuerConfirmed (enforced by allOf below) and optional otherwise — an inferred credit has no citation by definition, and requiring one would force either deleting unverified data or inventing a source for it.
